To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) situated agents acting as cultural conduits can explain the universal features of natural language; (2) situated agents acting in a cultural setting can explain the evolution of language structure; and, (3) the role of innativeness in explaining the universal features of human language is not as straightforward as is commonly believed.
The universal features of language are adaptive with respect to cultural transmission.
(1) the structure of language emerges as a result of the cultural transmission process, and (2) this process is facilitated by the innate predispositions of agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cultural transmission in explaining the universal features of human language.
the relationship between the structure of language and its function in social interaction.
understanding how the structure of human language can be explained in terms of the cognitive and social processes that underpin its use and transmission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the universal features of languages are the result of a combination of innate bias, cultural transmission, and the structure of the environment.
the universal features of human language are a product of the interaction between innate bias and cultural transmission.
the universal features of human language are the result of the interaction of innate biases with the cultural transmission of information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
language is a situated cognitive system that is subject to evolutionary forces.
we are not born knowing how to talk, but we are born knowing how to learn how to talk.
language is not only the product of innate biases and cultural learning, but that cultural learning itself is an important source of language structure and evolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
language structure is not specified at the level of individual agents but at the population level, as a result of a cultural evolutionary process.
the universal features of human language can be explained by a combination of innate bias and the process of cultural transmission.
the universal features of the language faculty are not necessarily specified in the brain, but rather emerge as a result of the interaction between innate bias and cultural transmission.
